name: Military rule: Buhari to Abubakar

summary.text: Sixteen years of military rule followed, almost all of it under Northern Muslim generals. Babangida annulled the election of 12 June 1993, which the Yoruba businessman M. K. O. Abiola had won. After a short interim government under the Yoruba Ernest Shonekan, Abacha seized power. Abubakar handed over to an elected government in 1999. In the 1990s the six geopolitical zones came into use for sharing out offices.

federal.text: Northern generals of several peoples (Fulani, Hausa and Kanuri) held power. In the South-West, the annulment of June 12 was felt as the denial of power to a Yoruba winner.

leaders.name: Muhammadu Buhari
leaders.title: Head of State
leaders.groupNote: Son of a Fulani chieftain; Hausa and Kanuri ancestry on his mother’s side.

leaders.name: Ibrahim Babangida
leaders.title: Military President
leaders.groupNote: Born in Minna. He told journalists and biographers that his immediate ancestors were Hausa from Kano (Kperogi). The owner’s list, and others, call him Gbagyi (Gwari); some say Nupe.

leaders.name: Sani Abacha
leaders.title: Head of State
leaders.groupNote: A Kanuri family from Borno, raised in Kano.

leaders.name: Abdulsalami Abubakar
leaders.title: Head of State
leaders.groupNote: Born in Minna, a city founded by the Gbagyi. He told a biographer he was born to Hausa parents (Kperogi); the owner’s list calls him Gbagyi and Hausa-speaking.

reviewNotes: Ethnic attributions follow the cited biographies. Where sources disagree, the leader is marked disputed and the alternatives are given.

parties.name: Social Democratic Party
parties.text: One of two parties the military created for the Third Republic. Its 1993 ticket paired Abiola, a Yoruba Muslim, with Baba Gana Kingibe, a Kanuri Muslim.

parties.name: National Republican Convention
parties.text: The other government-made party. Its 1993 candidate, Bashir Tofa of Kano, was little known outside his home state.

results.title: Presidential election, 12 June 1993
results.note: Annulled by Babangida before the results were declared in full. Abiola, a Yoruba, was later jailed and died in detention in 1998.

coups.name: The New Year’s Eve coup

plotters.name: Muhammadu Buhari
plotters.role: GOC 3rd Armoured Division, Jos; he denies taking part

killed.name: Ibrahim Bako
killed.role: Brigadier, killed by the President’s guards

coups.text: Officers ended the Second Republic on the last night of 1983. Shagari’s guards had been warned and fought back; Brigadier Bako, sent to arrest him, was killed. Buhari, like Shagari a Fulani from the North, became head of state.

moments.title: The plot reaches Jos
moments.text: According to Sambo Dasuki, plotters travel to Jos to brief Buhari, then commanding the 3rd Armoured Division. Buhari has denied any part in it.

moments.title: Firefight at the President’s villa
moments.text: Brigadier Bako arrives to arrest Shagari, but the Brigade of Guards had been warned. In the firefight Bako is killed.

moments.title: Buhari in power
moments.text: The Supreme Military Council returns, with Buhari as head of state and Idiagbon as his deputy.

coups.name: Babangida’s palace coup

rose.name: Ibrahim Babangida
rose.groupNote: His people are disputed: Hausa by his own account, Gbagyi by others.

coups.text: Babangida, Buhari’s own army chief, overthrew him from inside the regime, promising to fix the economy. Buhari was held in Benin City until 1988. Babangida called himself President and ruled through an Armed Forces Ruling Council, surviving coup attempts in 1986 and 1990.

moments.title: Babangida takes over
moments.text: Mid-level officers led by the Chief of Army Staff remove Buhari; the Supreme Military Council becomes the Armed Forces Ruling Council.

moments.title: Buhari detained
moments.text: The fallen head of state is held in Benin City until 1988.

coups.name: The Orkar coup attempt

fell.name: Ibrahim Babangida
fell.role: Military President, the target, who escaped

plotters.name: Gideon Orkar
plotters.groupNote: Of Tiv heritage, from Apir near Makurdi.

plotters.name: Anthony Nyiam
plotters.role: one of the plot’s real leaders, by the trial evidence

plotters.name: Saliba Mukoro
plotters.role: one of the plot’s real leaders

plotters.name: Cyril Obahor
plotters.role: one of the plot’s real leaders

coups.text: Officers speaking for the Niger Delta and the South attacked Dodan Barracks while Babangida was inside; he escaped by a back route. Their broadcast did more than end the regime: it announced the “excision” of five far-Northern states from Nigeria. Northern officers rallied to the government, the coup failed, and with the shoot-outs and executions it was the bloodiest in Nigeria’s history.

moments.title: Dodan Barracks attacked
moments.text: Rebels seize army headquarters and storm the presidential residence. Babangida escapes by a back route.

moments.title: The broadcast
moments.text: On Radio Nigeria Orkar accuses Babangida of planning to rule for life and the North of marginalising the Delta, and declares Bauchi, Borno, Katsina, Kano and Sokoto cut off from Nigeria.

moments.title: The executions
moments.text: Orkar and 41 others are executed by firing squad.

coups.areaLabel: The five states the broadcast “excised” (as drawn in 1990, now ten)

coups.name: Abacha takes over
coups.text: After Babangida annulled the June 1993 election, which Abiola, a Yoruba, had won, he left an interim government under Shonekan, another Yoruba. Within three months Abacha forced Shonekan out. He placed his rule above the courts and held power until his death in Abuja in June 1998.

moments.title: Shonekan out
moments.text: The Defence Minister, Abacha, forces the Interim President to resign and takes power.

moments.title: Abacha dies in office
moments.text: Abacha dies at the presidential villa; Abdulsalami Abubakar succeeds him and hands power to an elected government in 1999.
